Future Farming Five: what autonomous weeding taught Kilter

 01-10 | Smart farming | Article

LinkedInFacebookXWhatsAppPrint

AX-1 works best on small weeds, so treatment should start earlier than with broadcast spraying. Photos: Kilter

Kilter’s AX-1 robots apply herbicide in precise micro-droplets directly onto weeds, and have helped growers avoid spraying more than 1 million litres of herbicide mixture compared to what conventional broadcast spraying would have used. Future Farming asks the Norwegian company how this number was calculated, which growers benefit most from the AX-1, and what buyers should consider before investing.

1. AX-1 has helped farmers avoid spraying more than 1 million litres of herbicide mixture in under 8 months, across 5 countries. How did you arrive at this figure, and which type of growers or farm operations benefit most from AX-1’s technology today?

“The figure comes from telemetry data: AX-1 logs the number of droplets it applies, each 1 µL, giving the actual volume of herbicide mix used. That’s compared with what a conventional broadcast spray would have used on the same area, at a standard rate of 250 L/ha. Row crop growers with high-value vegetables benefit most, especially root vegetables and leafy greens. These are crops where weeds hit yield hard, herbicide options are limited, and manual weeding is expensive and hard to staff. Root vegetables have a long growth cycle, and keeping weeds under control all the way through it pays off at harvest: higher yield and a more even crop with fewer defects. Leafy greens are the opposite case but just as strong a fit. Fast growth and short cycles mean several crops per season and a narrow window for weed control, so precise, repeatable treatment pays off quickly. Kilter has both small and large farms as customers, and the technology scales well with the size of the operation. AX-1 is used on both flat fields and bed-formed fields.”

Anders Brevik, Managing Director at Kilter: “Root vegetables have a long growth cycle, and keeping weeds under control all the way through it pays off at harvest.”2. Beyond herbicide savings, what other measurable benefits are Kilter customers seeing – for example, in labour, yield, or soil health?

“The biggest one is yield. With up to 99% drift reduction, AX-1 can treat weeds right next to the crop plant, which is exactly where weeds compete hardest. And because the crop itself is not targeted, it avoids the herbicide stress that broadcast spraying causes. In our trials we have measured yield increases of 30 to 40%, along with more uniform growth and a higher share of marketable produce. Labour is the other major gain. AX-1 runs autonomously, freeing up hours that went into spraying or hand weeding in a sector where seasonal labour is scarce. We haven’t measured soil health effects yet, but reducing herbicide use by an average of 97% is naturally a step in the right direction.”

3. What is the biggest misconception growers have about autonomous weeding or spraying robots?

“That the robot makes the decisions. AX-1 takes over the repetitive, precise work in the field, but the agronomic judgement stays with the grower: which product to use, when to treat, and how to plan the season around it. Good planning matters just as much as before. What changes is that the plan gets executed with more precision. We believe no manual or broadcast method can match it. Timing is another thing growers sometimes get wrong. AX-1 works best on small weeds, so treatment should start earlier than with broadcast spraying. Treating early makes it possible to reduce volumes drastically. In slower-growing crops, new germination means the application has to be repeated, but the benefits clearly outweigh the extra passes.”

The Kilter fleet has logged approximately 20,000 hours of autonomous operation so far in 2026.4. What should every grower ask before investing in an autonomous machine like AX-1?

“How does it perform in my crop, my soil and my conditions, and can I see it running on a farm like mine? Who supports it locally when something goes wrong in the middle of the season? How does it fit my existing workflow, equipment and field layout? For AX-1, we have strong reference farms running it in large-scale operations, and our fleet has logged approximately 20,000 hours of autonomous operation so far in 2026, with the most heavily used machines passing 1,700 hours each. Local support is important, and comes through our distributors, Kubota in Europe and Croplands in Australia, so growers deal with a dealer network they already know.”

5. What do you expect AX-1 will be capable of 5 years from now that it cannot yet do today?

“That’s a question we prefer to answer with results rather than predictions. Development at Kilter is continuous, and AX-1 gets better through software updates and the experience we gain in the field. Our priorities are shaped by what growers need. What matters is what works reliably in their fields. When new capabilities are proven and ready, we’ll be happy to share them.””

translationZh:
**1. AX-1在不到8个月的时间里，横跨5个国家，帮助农民避免了超过100万升除草剂混合液的喷洒。你们是如何得出这个数字的？目前哪些类型的种植者或农场运营从AX-1技术中受益最大？**

“这个数字来自遥测数据：AX-1记录其施用的液滴数量，每个液滴为1微升，从而得出实际使用的除草剂混合液体积。然后将其与常规广播喷洒在相同面积上按标准用量250升/公顷所会使用的量进行比较。高价值蔬菜的row crop种植者受益最大，尤其是根茎类蔬菜和叶菜。这些作物中杂草对产量打击很大，除草剂选择有限，人工除草成本高昂且难以招到人手。根茎类蔬菜生长周期长，在整个周期内保持杂草控制，在收获时会有回报：更高的产量和更均匀的作物，缺陷更少。叶菜则相反，但同样非常适合。快速生长和短周期意味着每季可种多茬作物，杂草控制窗口很窄，因此精准、可重复的处理很快就能见效。Kilter既有小农场客户也有大农场客户，该技术能很好地随运营规模扩展。AX-1既可用于平田，也可用于起垄田。”

Kilter总经理Anders Brevik表示：“根茎类蔬菜生长周期长，在整个周期内保持杂草控制，在收获时会有回报。”

**2. 除了节省除草剂之外，Kilter客户还看到了哪些可衡量的好处——例如在劳动力、产量或土壤健康方面？**

“最大的是产量。凭借高达99%的漂移减少，AX-1可以在紧邻作物植株的地方处理杂草，而这正是杂草竞争最激烈的地方。而且由于作物本身不是目标，它避免了广播喷洒对作物造成的除草剂胁迫。在我们的试验中，我们测得产量增加了30%到40%，同时生长更均匀，可销售农产品的比例更高。劳动力是另一个主要收益。AX-1自主运行，释放了原本用于喷洒或人工除草的时间，而这个行业季节性劳动力稀缺。我们尚未测量土壤健康影响，但平均减少97%的除草剂使用量自然是朝着正确方向迈出的一步。”

**3. 种植者对自主除草或喷洒机器人最大的误解是什么？**

“认为机器人会做决定。AX-1接管了田间重复性、精确性的工作，但农艺判断仍由种植者掌握：使用什么产品、何时处理以及如何围绕它规划季节。好的规划与以前一样重要。改变的是计划执行得更精确。我们相信没有人工或广播方法能与之匹敌。时机是种植者有时会弄错的另一件事。AX-1对小杂草效果最好，因此处理应比广播喷洒更早开始。早期处理使得大幅减少用量成为可能。在生长较慢的作物中，新的发芽意味着必须重复施用，但好处显然超过了额外作业的成本。”

Kilter车队在2026年迄今已累计约20,000小时的自主运行时间。

**4. 在投资像AX-1这样的自主机器之前，每个种植者应该问什么？**

“它在我的作物、我的土壤和我的条件下表现如何，我能否在类似我的农场看到它运行？当季节中间出现问题时，谁在当地提供支持？它如何适应我现有的工作流程、设备和田块布局？对于AX-1，我们有强大的参考农场在大规模运营中使用它，我们的车队在2026年迄今已累计约20,000小时的自主运行时间，使用最频繁的机器每台超过1,700小时。本地支持很重要，通过我们的经销商提供，欧洲是Kubota，澳大利亚是Croplands，因此种植者与他们已经熟悉的经销商网络打交道。”

**5. 您预计AX-1在5年后能做到哪些今天还做不到的事情？**

“这个问题我们更愿意用结果而不是预测来回答。Kilter的开发是持续性的，AX-1通过软件更新和我们在田间获得的经验不断改进。我们的优先事项由种植者的需求决定。重要的是在他们的田地里可靠运行的东西。当新能力得到验证并准备就绪时，我们会乐于分享。”
